title: Palantir depth-5 controls, network and chronology assessment
summary: Depth-5 synthesis of IRS data controls, public ethics records, Rockbridge operating entities and 1789 investment-to-award timing.

data.question: What do the next-level technical controls, ethics records, legal operating entities and investment chronologies show about the Palantir–Thiel–Vance–Trump network?
data.method: Primary PIA extraction, public disclosure review, Form 990/FEC normalization and dated investment-versus-award comparison.
data.framework: control inheritance plus disclosure completeness plus operating-entity finance plus temporal causal discrimination
data.scope: Depth 5:IRS EDP controls; Barbaccia public ethics record; Rockbridge operating organizations; 1789 investment chronology.
findings: IRS EDP has documented identity, entitlement, waiver, contractor-screening, audit-logging, masking and filtering controls.
The public record does not establish that the new Unified API inherited the exact EDP control package, authorization boundary and consumer approvals.
Barbaccia disclosed PLTR, but the searched public record does not resolve disposition, ethics agreement, recusals, waivers or participation.
Rockbridge's operating layer includes separately registered nonprofits and a federal super PAC with materially different finances and legal duties.
Cerebras, PsiQuantum and Firehawk investment announcements followed the cited awards, weakening a theory that 1789 investment caused those awards.
Vulcan preserves a pre-award investment sequence:1789 participation in August 2025 preceded a November 2025 conditional federal loan commitment.
conclusions: The IRS branch now supports a control-inheritance investigation rather than a claim that no controls exist.
The Barbaccia branch remains a transparency and verification problem, not an established ethics violation.
The Rockbridge branch is a network of distinct legal vehicles rather than one balance sheet.
Vulcan is the highest-priority 1789 chronology because its investment predates the major federal financing event.
counterarguments: Existing EDP controls may fully apply to Unified API even where the public award record does not specify them.
Barbaccia may have disposed of PLTR or received nonpublic ethics instructions.
Shared leadership and reported affiliation do not prove common ownership.
Vulcan's financing may have been selected solely on industrial-policy and technical merits.
limitations: Unified API statement of work and authorization package were not public in reviewed sources.
Agency ethics records can be nonpublic or held outside OGE's central public repository.
501(c)(4) donor identities are generally not public.
Private investment stake sizes and internal communications remain undisclosed.

No public record reviewed establishes an ethics violation.
